newsitem.title: USA: TEMIC sees 1997 U.S. revenue growth.
newsitem.headline: TEMIC sees 1997 U.S. revenue growth.

text.p: TEMIC, the electronics unit of German industrial giant Daimler-Benz AG, said Monday it expects its total U.S. revenues to grow by 25 percent in 1997, to about 500 million marks ($299 million).

In 1996, TEMIC said its Automotive Electronic Business Unit's worldwide revenues increased by 30 percent world-wide. In 1997, the unit's revenues are expected to grow by an additional 35 percent and will reach a turnover of 1 billion marks ($598 million).

The company announced its projections at the Society of Automotive Engineers' annual convention here and added that the U.S. projection also includes results from semiconductors and non-automotive micro-electronics.

"The North American market is playing more and more an important role for our Automotive Electronics business," TEMIC management board chairman Frank Dieter Maier said in a statement. "Here we are growing faster than the market."
In 1997, TEMIC said its U.S. revenues from anti-lock braking system (ABS) electronics will increase by 60 percent, amounting to 150 million marks ($89.7 million).

The company attributed the increase mainly to a contract recently awarded to it by ITT Automotive, a unit of ITT Industries Inc. The new contract results from two big orders from Ford Motor Co and Chrysler Corp for new ITT ABS systems, yielding an additional order volume to TEMIC of 50 million marks ($29.9 million) per year.

TEMIC also said the 1997 ABS revenue increases include new ABS contracts for Mercedes-Benz' new U.S.-built M-Class sport/utility vehicle and Volkswagen AG's new beetle, which will be produced in Mexico.

TEMIC said its new plant in Cuautla, Mexico, is increasing its capacity to produce two million ABS modules per year. The plant, which employs 1,300 people, produces products for the entire NAFTA trading region.

In 1996, TEMIC's total revenues for all business units reached 2.5 billion marks ($1.495 billion) with 10,900 employees worldwide. A company spokesman declined to offer a projection for the company's 1997 total revenues.
